items.summary: Supplementary methods, results, data tables and analysis code for the manuscript Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity. The five resources contain supplementary methods, tables and figures, detailed data workbooks, reproducibility code and supporting audit documentation. Original code is licensed under MIT; original documentation and derived content are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their source terms; see LICENSES.md and source notices inside Online_Resource_3.zip. Manuscript abstract Public intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) datasets cover different tissue compartments and measure different subsets of genes, complicating comparisons across studies. We compared four specified gene sets (inflammation, complement, microglial activation and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated oxidative stress) in public paired human brain, single-cell and hematoma-effluent/blood datasets, using patients rather than cells as inferential units. In two studies of paired brain tissue, inflammation, complement and NRF2-associated scores were higher in perihematomal than contralateral samples in all four patient blocks and five matched pairs. Patient-level single-cell comparisons found higher inflammatory and complement scores in microglia/monocyte groups than in comparator lineages. In 14 patients with same-hour paired CD14+ and neutrophil data, a five-gene score named for microglial activation showed a positive CD14+–neutrophil local-response interaction in all 14 (adjusted P=0.000488), but four-program heterogeneity was not established (Friedman P=0.0796). Restricting this score to three shared genes reversed its CD14+ local response; a jointly scaled three-gene interaction was near zero. Independent acute blood data showed positive case-control differences, whereas longitudinal changes were not significant after adjustment. Inflammatory and NRF2-associated expression differences recurred across these datasets. The CD14+ local response of the microglial-related score depended on its measured genes. items.summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.

items.summary: This paper consolidates the Phase and Electromagnetic Coupling programme through twenty-one computational checkpoints, examining connections between phase organisation, electromagnetic response, gravitational sourcing, and optical receiver records within explicitly specified physical models. The analysis connects amplitude and relative phase to internal-state geometry, collective quantum electromagnetic responses, material currents, and the complete stress–energy tensor of a relativistic scalar field. It distinguishes the information contained in a joint source state from the information accessible through a particular coupling, including collective bright and dark responses that cannot be recovered from separate local states alone. In the gravitational calculations, two internal phase arrangements with matching initial local current, stress, and geometry subsequently produce different neutral-probe tidal responses. A specified optical construction carries a selected difference into receiver-clock intervals, radar distance, and interference signals. The response persists in an independently solved zero-charge family, demonstrating that an electromagnetic source field is not required for this particular modelled gravitational phase dependence. The paper also establishes a restricted mathematical connection between the programme’s nested gravitational source proposal and conventional field stress. An amplitude-weighted cosine expression appears as the equal-amplitude, single-component limit of a squared transported field difference. Retaining amplitude variation, internal-state overlap, and directional and temporal information permits reconstruction of the complete source and its gravitational accounting. Foundational Phase remains nonspatial in the proposed interpretation; coordinates and dynamics belong to the represented coupling description. The results are conditional mathematical correspondences and numerical findings using supplied interactions, Maxwell equations, Einstein gravity, and ideal receiver laws. Physical source identification, dimensional calibration, and measured receiver response remain open. The quantum and classical calculations are separate models, with no quantum-to-classical derivation claimed. The accompanying reproducibility release contains the synthesis, branch master, twenty-one checkpoint reports, original computational packages, and a catalogue linking results to their verification procedures.

items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.
items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

items.summary: The same upper central incisor in every panel, cut from the lip side to the palate side, with the gum, ligament and bone around it. The tooth and the tissues at its neck are drawn to published measurements; the break, the etched enamel, the key and the layers show what typically happens, not one patient's tooth. Sources The rebuild follows two principles from one textbook. The additive principle: in a direct restoration the etching and bonding are extended beyond the defect onto intact enamel, to blend and reinforce the restoration; its example is a small chipped edge restored without preparation: the tooth was etched, bonded and restored well beyond the fracture line under rubber dam. And natural guided stratification: a silicone index made from a wax-up or mock-up holds a palatal shell of enamel-like material, dentine-like increments are placed where the natural dentine was, and the last increment is the labial enamel. Magne and Belser 2022, Biomimetic Restorative Dentistry, volume 1, pages 319, 330 and 331. In 455 crown-fractured permanent incisors followed for a mean of 2.3 years and up to 17, the pulp survived in 99 per cent of teeth the injury had not also loosened or displaced, and in none of them did it die; when the tooth had also been loosened, pulp death in fractures through enamel and dentine, like this one, rose from 0 to 28 per cent. Robertson et al. 2000, International Journal of Paediatric Dentistry. https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1365-263x.2000.00191.x A 2024 German clinical guideline on direct composite restorations, agreed by strong consensus, recommends etching the enamel of every direct composite restoration with phosphoric acid, to improve the long-term quality of the enamel margin and prevent discoloration there. It finds both rubber dam and other isolation workable, with rubber dam possibly helping restorations last longer. These process recommendations are consensus-based. Sekundo et al. 2024, The Journal of Adhesive Dentistry, part 2. https://doi.org/10.3290/j.jad.b5749192 Acid on the enamel only, before a universal adhesive: in a randomised trial of 295 back-tooth fillings in 70 patients, fillings bonded this way showed significantly fewer defects at their edges after 24 months than those bonded with the adhesive alone. Barceleiro et al. 2023, Journal of Applied Oral Science. https://doi.org/10.1590/1678-7757-2022-0323 In fillings at the necks of teeth, a meta-analysis of 10 randomised trials found less staining and fewer adaptation defects at the edges when the enamel was etched selectively before a self-etch adhesive, and fewer fillings lost at three years. Szesz et al. 2016, Journal of Dentistry, systematic review and meta-analysis. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jdent.2016.05.009 A Cochrane review of six randomised trials with 1,342 participants found low-certainty evidence that rubber dam may lower the failure rate of fillings compared with cotton rolls at six months, and very uncertain evidence at other times; all the trials were at high risk of bias, and the results came from fillings at the necks of teeth and in children's back teeth. Miao et al. 2021, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD009858.pub3 A meta-analysis of 21 prospective clinical trials of front-tooth composites estimated that 90 per cent of Class IV restorations, which rebuild a broken corner or edge of a front tooth, last 10 years without being replaced; bulk fracture was the main reason for replacement, more often with microfilled composites. Twelve of the trials started before 1991. items.summary: Associated manuscript: Bounded residual plasticity reduces negative transfer in adaptive motor-imagery EEG decoding. This release archives the numerical analyses, configuration records and figures used to evaluate bounded residual adaptation in motor-imagery EEG decoding. The architecture retains the source encoder and classifier and confines participant-specific adaptation to a rank-2 latent residual with a 2% source-probe displacement bound. The cohort-stratified combined analysis included 109 PhysioNet participants evaluated on held-out tasks and nine BCI Competition IV-2a participants evaluated cross-dataset. Negative transfer exceeding one percentage point in at least one subsequent evaluation session occurred in 5/118 participants under bounded residual adaptation, compared with 33/118 under unconstrained encoder adaptation and 25/118 under hard-KL adaptation. Mean bounded residual utility was −0.042 percentage points. An additional EEGNet-style raw-EEG robustness analysis involving 109 PhysioNet participants found 5/109 negative-transfer events for bounded adaptation and 22/109 for unconstrained adaptation. Included records: Cohort-stratified statistical summaries, paired contingency tables, raw-EEG participant-by-method results, configuration and provenance records, parameter-update summaries, figures and a Python numerical verification script. The numerical verification can be run using: python scripts/verify_results.py Reproducibility scope: This archive supports verification of the recorded statistical comparisons and recomputation of the supplementary raw-EEG event counts. The original EEG preprocessing and training pipelines, primary participant-level results and model checkpoints are not included. Complete end-to-end model retraining requires those original project assets. items.summary: HBB2OBB converts horizontal (axis-aligned) bounding boxes (HBBs) into oriented (rotated) bounding boxes (OBBs) by using existing HBB annotations as prompts for segmentation models from the SAM (Segment Anything Model) family. It targets object detection tasks where objects appear at arbitrary orientations, such as aerial imagery, satellite data, and traffic monitoring, producing oriented boxes that tightly encapsulate non-upright objects without any re-annotation. Beyond conversion, it provides horizontal box detection, evaluation, hyperparameter optimization, an interactive annotation viewer, and annotation format-conversion tools, exposed through both a command-line interface and a Python API. 📖 Documentation: rfonod.github.io/hbb2obb , with a quick start on the bundled sample data, a guide per command, pages on how the conversion works, the confidence score, the metrics and provenance, and a CLI and API reference generated from the code. Why HBB2OBB 🎯 Accurate OBBs from HBBs : prompts SAM-family segmentation models with existing horizontal boxes to fit tight oriented boxes around non-upright objects, with no re-annotation required. 🚗 No HBBs? Detect them : the hbb2obb-detect command runs an Ultralytics detector over the images and writes the horizontal boxes the conversion consumes, confidence column included. 🧩 Model ensemble : combines masks from multiple SAM variants through majority voting for more robust, accurate results. 🛡️ Spatially constrained and safe : region-specific masking and contour refinement keep segmentation inside the object, a mask split by an occluder is fitted back together, and a fallback retains the original HBB when no valid mask is found, counted and reported rather than left to be discovered afterwards. 🔎 Confidence-scored output : every OBB receives a heuristic quality score in [0, 1] that flags silent fallbacks and low-confidence conversions, so you know which boxes to trust; the scores go in the label files or in a side-car directory that keeps them strictly standard, and the detector's own confidence can be carried through instead of, or on top of, that score. 📐 Flexible scaling : positive or negative scale factors, optionally different for the short and long sides, recover cropped object parts or tighten overly conservative annotations. 📊 Evaluate and optimize : evaluation against ground truth on IoU, orientation error, and the share of boxes above a high IoU bar, plus the hbb2obb-optimize command, a hyperparameter search over SAM inference resolution, scale factors, and morphological opening kernel, driven by a configuration file so that a whole benchmark of model ensembles is a single reproducible command. 🔬 Where the score comes from : the hbb2obb-analyze command breaks one evaluation down by the ground truth's orientation, size, frame edge, difficulty and class, and scores the conversion against emitting the horizontal prompt unchanged. 🔄 Five annotation formats : read and write YOLO, DOTA, Pascal VOC, COCO, and LabelMe, for horizontal and oriented boxes alike, with a check that proves every format encodes the same boxes. 🔍 Interactive viewer : the hbb2obb-view command pans and zooms over the annotations, in any format, coloring boxes by confidence and overlaying predictions against ground truth. items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.
items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs. Data availability and reproducibility The original datasets are available from their respective third-party providers, subject to their applicable access and reuse conditions. The frozen intervention texts used for the C0–C3 experiments are not redistributed in this public software archive. Their SHA-256 integrity manifest is provided to support verification of authorised copies. Consequently, complete reproduction of text-dependent experiments requires access to the original datasets and the frozen intervention texts. The public archive supports inspection of the methodology and reproduction of analyses for which the necessary inputs or saved instance-level outputs are included. Scope and limitations The reported intervention experiments did not execute pretrained DistilBERT, RoBERTa or DeBERTa baselines. Independent clinical semantic-equivalence adjudication of the generated transformations was not completed. The results are computational and do not establish clinical deployment performance. This record accompanies the associated research manuscript and is intended to support transparent reporting, methodological scrutiny and further replication.

The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs. Data availability and reproducibility The original datasets are available from their respective third-party providers, subject to their applicable access and reuse conditions. The frozen intervention texts used for the C0–C3 experiments are not redistributed in this public software archive. Their SHA-256 integrity manifest is provided to support verification of authorised copies. Consequently, complete reproduction of text-dependent experiments requires access to the original datasets and the frozen intervention texts. The public archive supports inspection of the methodology and reproduction of analyses for which the necessary inputs or saved instance-level outputs are included. items.summary: Preservation copy of an article published in International Journal of Science, Technology and Management . Read the full article: https://ioro.org/ijstm/article/705694772108/705694772108 . Organizations increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve strategic planning, operational efficiency, and sustainability. However, conventional machine learning models often lack transparency, limiting managerial trust, accountability, and the practical adoption of AI-driven decisions. This study proposes an explainable AI (XAI) framework that integrates predictive analytics, interpretable machine learning, and sustainability indicators to support transparent, reliable, and evidence-based decision-making across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Evaluation uses a benchmark dataset containing operational performance, resource consumption, organizational efficiency, and environmental indicators. Comparative experiments assess predictive accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), explanation consistency, decision latency, computational cost, and sustainability performance. Baseline models include Logistic Regression, conventional Random Forest, and XGBoost without explanation mechanisms. Ablation studies examine the individual contributions of interpretability and sustainability-aware optimization. The experimental evaluation is designed to determine whether the proposed framework improves predictive reliability, explanation quality, and sustainability-aware decisions compared with conventional approaches. Quantitative reporting will include percentage improvements in predictive performance, reductions in decision latency and resource consumption, and explanation stability across repeated experiments. Qualitative analysis will assess managerial understandability, perceived trustworthiness, fairness, and practical implementation challenges. Numerical outcomes will be reported only after experiments are completed, avoiding unsupported performance claims. The proposed framework establishes a comparative approach for integrating explainability, predictive intelligence, and sustainability into organizational decision-making. By connecting model predictions with transparent explanations and measurable sustainability indicators, the framework aims to strengthen accountability, operational effectiveness, and responsible technology adoption. Future validation across multiple industries will establish its generalizability and practical value.

items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.
items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

items.summary: This dataset is the supplementary material for the manuscript "Decision Neutrality of Forecast Revisions in Microgrids with Photovoltaics and Battery Storage" by Yun Xing (Hohai University), submitted to Applied Sciences (MDPI). Version 1.0, 25 October 2026. Overview The study asks when adopting a revised next-day forecast changes a battery dispatch decision, rather than only the predicted cost. It derives two checkable sufficient reset conditions under which old and revised forecasts produce next-day storage value functions that differ only by an additive constant. A fixed-input perturbation bound separates this local neutrality from realized rolling-policy performance. Five policies (FF, FS, SF, SS and DAY) are compared on 522 community-days from 270 measured households aggregated into nine synthetic communities, with three synthetic tariffs and two import regimes. Key results - Freezing next-day forecasts is numerically neutral under unlimited imports across the tested tariffs. - Under a 30 kW import cap and time-of-use pricing, retaining midnight targets (DAY) lowers total operating cost by 3.105% relative to full updating (FF). Lower unmet-demand penalties account for 88.3% of the reduction; the import-bill reduction is 0.588%. - Freezing both forecasts while replanning (SS) costs 0.054% more than FF under the same six-hour replanning schedule, separating forecast adoption from target retention. - Under the same cap and tariff, freezing only the next-day forecast (FS) costs 0.188% more than FF. - Matched-calendar comparisons show that the magnitude of update effects depends on the controller scheme. items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.
